new_statements.quote: 1.2 Typological profile[.] Maaka is a tone language with two tone levels (high, low) and two contour tones (falling, rising), in which tone has a salient lexical role, but also fulfils grammatical functions. Maaka can be characterized as a weakly agglutinating language, with a tendency to compensate the absence of Chadic morphology by innovative compounding strategies (Coly forthcoming).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Maaka is described as a two-level tone language (H, L, plus falling and rising contours) with lexical and grammatical tone; no source seen makes any statement about word stress or accent. Schuh's open Maka Wordlist (saved) independently transcribes every elicited item with H/L/falling tone and vowel length and likewise says nothing about stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Typological-profile statement about the lexical/grammatical tone system; not a statement about word-level prominence. Text read via Google Books snippet only; the remainder of sec. 1.2 (which might mention syllable structure or stress) was not visible.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same language, glottocode maak1236 (no dialect codes in Glottolog). Newman 1965's speaker was from Gulani ('Maha', medial [h]); Schuh's 2007 consultants were from Bara ('Maka' [maaka], medial [k]); Suzzi Valli 2014 (per Baldi's review) distinguishes Bara and Gulani dialects. The fieldwork base of Storch & Coly was not visible in the snippet.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. n.d. [data collected 6 Aug 2007]. Maka Wordlist. UCLA Department of Linguistics, Yobe Languages Research Project (NSF BCS-0553222). 10 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Intro p.2 treats the language as tonal: 'Almost all the entries from our session are marked for tone and vowel length (macron = long vowel, grave accent (à) = low tone, circumflex accent (â) = falling tone, no accent (a) = high tone).' Also discusses lateral fricatives and verb classes; ~150 tone-marked items plus Newman 1965 items.
